title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused rope/rotary ops + scheduling tweaks for continuous batching
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: This PR upgrades the attention kernels in the runtime to use FlashAttentionV2 variants with fused rotary/rope ops and adds scheduling and KV-cache alignment changes to improve continuous batching throughput and memory efficiency. The goal is to reduce p99 latency for short requests, increase sustained throughput for multi-tenant workloads, and lower peak GPU memory to enable larger batch sizes without violating SLOs.

Summary of changes: - Introduce FlashAttentionV2 kernels tuned for Redwood layouts and fused rope/rotary ops to avoid separate elementwise kernels. This reduces memory traffic and kernel launch overhead. - Add fused qkv pack/unpack path and optional packed QKV kernel for models that benefit (saves allocation/transpose ops). - KV cache alignment and compacted storage format to reduce footprint for long-context models; adds a runtime converter for older checkpoints. - Scheduling heuristics for continuous batching: request-size-aware worker assignment, early-batch release thresholds, and adaptive batch size caps. These heuristics reduce head-of-line blocking when mixed short/long requests compete. - Feature flag and fallback: runtime will fall back to legacy attention kernels on unsupported GPUs or when deterministic mode is requested. - Tests: microbenchmarks (latency and throughput harness), end-to-end correctness tests for rotary/rope equivalence, KV cache regression tests, and a canary perf rollout script.

Benchmarks (NVIDIA A100 80GB, mixed workloads): - Short chat (seq_len 64): p50 latency -7%, p95 latency -9%, p99 latency -12% vs previous FlashAttentionV1-based runtime. - Long context (seq_len 4096): sustained throughput +18% tokens/s, GPU memory peak -10%. - Multi-tenant continuous batching (50/50 short/long mix): tail latency p99 -20%, achieved 1.3x effective throughput due to reduced head-of-line blocking.

Compatibility and rollout: The new kernels are behind the feature flag runtime.enable_flashv2 and an environment flag ATTENTION_KERNEL=flashv2_fused. Default remains legacy for conservative rollout. We performed a staged canary on dedicated and hosted fleets; the PR includes a canary script to automate metrics collection and automatic rollback on error budget breaches.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation (CUDA/C++) - [x] Runtime scheduler changes + unit tests - [x] KV cache format migration path + tests - [x] Microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf harness - [x] Docs: runtime flags and rollout notes - [x] CI: build and integration tests pass

Notes: The PR touches performance-sensitive code paths; reviewers should focus on memory alignment details in redwood/runtime/attention/kv_cache.h and correctness of rope/rotary fusion in redwood/runtime/attention/rope_fused_ops.cu. We intentionally kept the new kernels as drop-in alternatives so rolling back is a config change, not a code revert.

Related: previous work on FlashAttention upgrades in pr-40321 and pr-45901; this PR combines fused-ops ideas from those forks and adds scheduling + KV-cache compaction to realize end-to-end perf for continuous batching workloads.
